items.title: Ray Vega interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 20, 2023
items.q: I recently played with Roy McCurdy, his last drummer. I did a West Coast thing with him up the Pacific Northwest.

ctx.x: Yeah, yeah, yeah. I recently played with Roy McCurdy, his last drummer. I did a West Coast thing with him up the Pacific Northwest. We talked about all of that stuff. You connect with the audience. It’s important that we do that. And that doesn’t mean that we’re not presenting art music because it is art music. But let them see the humanity of the musician on stage. Unless you are just so so so shy that you can’t speak. I get it. But we don’t talk to our students about that. I talk to my students about, because I…

that band like a band and I oversee the rehearsal. And these kids, first things first. Maybe one or two of them are music majors, the rest of them are engineers, astrophysicists, neuroscientists, all sorts of stuff. And these cats are on the case. We just graduated a young woman trombonist, an anthropology major. But she was a double major in music. So we got these kids that are coming in that are really brilliant but I have them develop the sets. And then when we’re going to do a recital I tell them okay now…
